A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Metformin potentiates nephrotoxicity by promoting NETosis in response to renal ferroptosis.
evidence_quotes: we treated mice with AKI induced by renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) with different drugs alone.
a higher dose of metformin (200 mg/kg) resulted in 100% lethality of I/R mice while the untreated I/R mice showed 100% survival (Fig. 1h).

C_secondary_contextual.title: The Gehan test identifies life-extending compounds overlooked by the log-rank test in the NIA Interventions Testing Program: Metformin, Enalapril, caffeic acid phenethyl ester, green tea extract, and 17-dimethylaminoethylamino-17-demethoxygeldanamycin hydrochloride.
evidence_quotes: Metformin at 1000 ppm starting at 9 months increased the median lifespan of males by 8% (Fig. 1C), but this effect did not reach statistical significance using the log-rank test [9].
The National Institute on Aging Interventions Testing Program (ITP) has so far identified 12 compounds that extend the lifespan of genetically heterogeneous mice using the log-rank test.
demote_reasons: no quote names a control term

C_secondary_contextual.title: Metformin improves healthspan and lifespan in mice.
evidence_quotes: Cohorts of middle-aged male C57BL/6 and B6C3F1 mice were provided with either a standard diet (SD) or SD supplemented with 0.1% (w/w) or 1% (w/w) metformin for the remainder of their lives.
Diet supplementation with 0.1% metformin led to a 5.83% extension of mean lifespan (Fig. 1a), w2 = 5.46 and P = 0.02 in Gehan–Breslow survival test.
demote_reasons: no quote names a control term

C_secondary_contextual.title: Metformin extends the lifespan of iMSUD mice by rescuing physiologic dysfunction and modulating mechanisms of mTORC1 activation
evidence_quotes: we next treated iMSUD mice with different doses of metformin by daily intra-peritoneal (IP) injection started at 5 days of age.

The survival is dose-dependently increased at a higher dose (250 mg/ kg bw) of metformin with a median survival of 32 days (metformin-treated) vs 24 days (PBS-treated) in females and a median survival of 33 days (metformin-treated) vs 24 days (PBS-treated) males
demote_reasons: no quote names a control term

C_secondary_contextual.title: Effect of Metformin on Cardiac Metabolism and Longevity in Aged Female Mice.
C_secondary_contextual.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
evidence_quotes: To this end, we set to investigate the role of Met treatment in female mice.
Surprisingly, rather than the life-extending effect, we found a significantly shortened lifespan in aged female mice receiving long-term Met supplementation vs . age-matched controls.
